skill.name: face-swap
skill.description: Route consented face and character swaps for still images and video through the RunComfy CLI. It selects model endpoints for still images, batch identity edits, character animation, and motion transfer.
skill.summary: Choose the right RunComfy route for consented image and video face swaps.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The pattern-based Ruby backtick, hardcoded URL, hidden-file, and reconnaissance findings are false positives from Markdown documentation and scoped RunComfy CLI usage. Semantic review found a high-risk dual-use identity-swap workflow because consent checks are advisory, and a medium privacy risk because biometric media is processed by third-party endpoints.

remediation.issue: Consent and misuse controls are advisory only.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required preflight consent checklist and refusal rules for public figures, sexual content, defamation, fraud, and political impersonation.

remediation.issue: Sensitive face, video, and audio inputs are sent to external model endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose third-party processing clearly, require user-provided assets, recommend short-lived signed URLs, and document retention expectations.

remediation.issue: CLI use depends on local credentials and output downloads.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the tool scope restricted to Bash(runcomfy *), verify token file permissions, and keep output directories user-selected and non-sensitive.

semantic_findings.title: Unenforced Dual-Use Identity Swap Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill is explicitly designed for face swap, character swap, and deepfake-style identity substitution. It warns that the model API will run supplied inputs and relies on operator refusal rather than an enforceable consent gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly advertises identity substitution triggers and states that the skill does not gate inputs. The consent guidance is present but implemented only as prose.

semantic_findings.title: Biometric Media Sent to Third-Party Processing
semantic_findings.description: The routes send face images, video, and audio URLs to RunComfy model endpoints and download generated outputs. Those inputs can contain biometric and voice data, so users need clear consent, retention, and access-control handling.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command examples and how-it-works section show user media being processed through external RunComfy APIs. The risk is transparent and intended, but it is still material for sensitive identity data.

content.user_title: Route Consented Face Swaps with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Users need to choose the right RunComfy route for consented identity edits across images and videos. This skill maps the request to the correct model endpoint and CLI input pattern.
actual_capabilities: Routes still image face swaps to GPT Image 2 Edit, Nano Banana Edit, or Flux Kontext.
Routes video character swaps to Wan 2-2 Animate or Kling Motion Control Pro.
Provides RunComfy CLI command examples and input fields for each route.
Explains when to choose motion preservation, batch consistency, or single-shot fidelity.
Includes consent, disclosure, shell-safety, endpoint, and token-storage guidance.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI installation, authentication, and access to external RunComfy model endpoints.
Does not technically verify identity rights or consent; the operator must enforce policy.
Input quality and model behavior affect identity match, lighting, and motion accuracy.
Third-party processing requires careful handling of sensitive biometric media.

use_cases.title: Create Consented Campaign Stills
use_cases.description: A creative team can place an approved spokesperson face into one hero image while preserving the scene and lighting.

use_cases.title: Prepare Character Motion Tests
use_cases.description: A video editor can transfer a reference performance onto an approved character image for motion review.

use_cases.title: Batch Identity-Consistent Drafts
use_cases.description: An ecommerce designer can test the same approved identity across several product or narrative frames.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Safe Route
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner route selection for a consented edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have consent to edit this identity. Help me choose the best RunComfy route for one still image face swap.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Still Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Build instructions for a precise still image swap.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a RunComfy plan for a consented portrait-to-scene face swap. Preserve pose, clothing, background, and lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Video Character Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Select between animation and motion transfer routes.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have permission for both assets. Compare Wan 2-2 Animate and Kling Motion Control for this video character swap.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Advanced Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for multiple images and disclosure needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my consented batch face-swap workflow for route choice, input order, disclosure labels, privacy risks, and output checks.

output_examples.input: A user has an approved portrait and one campaign scene still.
output_examples.output: Recommended route: GPT Image 2 Edit. Use the scene as the primary image, the portrait as the identity reference, and preserve lighting and background.

output_examples.input: A user has an approved character image and a source performance video.
output_examples.output: Recommended route: Kling Motion Control Pro. It is best when source motion and blocking must be preserved.

output_examples.input: A user has one approved identity reference and several product frames.
output_examples.output: Recommended route: Nano Banana Edit. Put the identity reference first and keep the same aspect ratio and resolution across the batch.

best_practices: Confirm identity rights, asset rights, and platform disclosure requirements before any swap.
Use only media URLs that the user explicitly provided for the current task.
Review outputs for identity accuracy, lighting mismatch, consent scope, and required synthetic media labels.
anti_patterns: Do not process real people, public figures, sexual content, defamation, fraud, or impersonation without clear consent.
Do not paste untrusted prompts or asset URLs into a shell command outside the RunComfy input boundary.
Do not use long-lived public URLs for sensitive face, voice, or video assets.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It routes consented face and character swaps to the appropriate RunComfy model endpoint.

faq.question: Does it verify consent automatically?
faq.answer: No. The operator must confirm rights, consent, and allowed use before running any workflow.

faq.question: Can it work with still images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes routes for single stills, batches, character animation, and motion transfer.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: It requires the RunComfy CLI, authentication, and access to the selected RunComfy model APIs.

faq.question: Where does processing happen?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI sends input media URLs to RunComfy model endpoints and downloads generated outputs.

faq.question: When should a request be refused?
faq.answer: Refuse requests involving nonconsensual real people, harmful impersonation, sexual content, defamation, fraud, or missing disclosure.
